title: Research: extra factors do not lower the fixed P112 COPY-power optimum
head: 8051d99dfd91a788d25bfc92c3863a33c658a5a9
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

For the fixed PR #2021 P112 two-column completion with ports `(0,1)` and coefficient `+1`, the sharp separate COPY-power minimum remains

`7*8^q + 7^q + 1`, for every `0<q<=1`,

when **any finite number of complex rank-one terms is allowed and both factors stay in the completion's minimal nine-dimensional column and row spaces**. COPY has sharp minimum 64. For `q<1`, the minimum is still strictly above `8*8^q`.

This extends Hanhong Zhao's [PR #2321](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2321), which covers exactly nine terms. Its support catalogue and rational attainer are credited and reconstructed independently. The new proof replaces termwise nine-dimensional duality with an eight-dimensional projection argument when exactly eight terms are mixed, and a rank-three bound on the aggregate cost-seven contribution when more terms are mixed. A compensation argument allows arbitrary numbers of pure terms, including nonzero zero-COPY terms.

The new package is `research/p112-overcomplete-factor-spaces/`. It contains the proof, exact certificate, verifier, source pins and registered replay. An eleven-term in-space fixture attains the bound with two nonzero zero-COPY terms. A ten-term boundary fixture in the one-dimensional right-space extension `col(R)+Ce_0` has profile `(8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,0,0)`, demonstrating that the factor-space restriction is essential for the power bound.

This is a **scoped proof supported by finite certificates**, not an unrestricted masked-decoder barrier, physical supplier, completed moment, or κ improvement. Native frames, arbitrary-dirty realization, shared COPY work, precision, reserve, hosting and all-size transfer remain unchecked. The written universal argument is not formally verified or independently human-reviewed.

## Validation

Python 3.12.3, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-overcomplete-factor-spaces --check-only
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-overcomplete-factor-spaces
```

Both pass. The mathematical finite-premise replay reports:

```text
PASS_P112_OVERCOMPLETE_FACTOR_SPACES kernels=1022 class_pairs=132 entries=12544 COPY=64 controls=7
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/p112-overcomplete-factor-spaces outcome=negative-result
```

Coverage includes SHA256 and Gram/binary source binding; exact rational kernels and intersections; both direct-support and span-based binary rank elimination; 12,544-entry comparisons for each factorization fixture; and exact integer partial-sum comparisons, without sampling `q`.

Seven rejection controls cover altered factors, omitted compensation, V/V undercharge, changed source bytes, a changed character premise, substitution of Hermitian transpose, and an undercharged certificate. A nonreal Gaussian-integer phase fixture passes with ordinary transpose.

A minimal relocated source export also passed `python3 -I -OO -B <export>/research/p112-overcomplete-factor-spaces/verify.py` from a different working directory, preserving every input/package hash. Mutating the actual exported source or certificate was rejected. The combined portability/mutation check took 4.36 seconds. The normal verifier is read-only; evidence regeneration uses exclusive creation and refuses to overwrite.

The selected-result binding check and the card's local-word ceiling positive control passed during orientation. The selected full cold replay was not run because the selected construction is unchanged. No Lean build, external-agent proof review or hosted-CI success is claimed. `git diff --check` and reverse patch applicability passed.

The registered replay was run again on the final package bytes before submission, under an 8 GiB memory cap: it passed in about two seconds and left the worktree unchanged. The optimum matches the exactly-nine-term value (COPY 64 at q = 1); this account's PR #2385 covers the complementary question of other nonzero coefficients at exactly nine terms.

## Open next questions

The package's `TASK.json` and README specify two follow-ups:

1. Classify the single extra right dimension `col(R)+Ce_0` and ask whether this fixed completion admits a power bill below `8*8^q`. The exact ten-term boundary supplies the first control. The present character catalogue does not cover the extension.
2. Specify one legal construction that shares COPY work across terms, then charge frames, restoration, precision and reserve. Separate support billing is an explicit theorem premise; no physical implementation is supplied here.
